condition: unilateral resting right hand tremor and slow shuffling gait in both legs over 8 months in an older adult
level_rationale: An 8-month history of unilateral resting right-hand tremor accompanied by a slow shuffling gait in both legs in a 68-year-old adult is a classic presentation of degenerative parkinsonism warranting neurology specialist evaluation and dopaminergic management, whereas both legs suddenly going limp under the patient when walking represents acute bilateral lower-extremity paraparesis requiring immediate emergency department spinal and neurovascular evaluation.

Both legs move in slow shuffling steps when walking

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + unsourced normal-aging causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact bilateral lower-extremity motor escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 68, 8 months of right-hand shaking at rest, and slow shuffling steps in both legs when walking) without naming Parkinson disease, with a 2-word span difference (18 vs 20 words), zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets across all 6 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, escalating only f3 on the exact same 'both my legs ... when walking' frame from chronic slow shuffling steps to suddenly going limp under the speaker keeps the 8-month resting hand tremor fully coherent while shifting care cleanly from neurology specialist evaluation (level 3) to emergency department evaluation (level 4).
